title: Non-elevated install failing on scheduled task registration
notes: Tool failure -> root cause -> fix -> verification -> a second related gap found.

turns.text: The service install step is failing on this machine with 'Access is denied' when it tries to register the scheduled task.
That's schtasks requiring elevation for some task configurations. Let me check what our install script actually needs...
We specifically wanted this to work non-elevated per the hardening work.

Right, I see — the XML task definition had <RunLevel>HighestAvailable</RunLevel>, which forces elevation even for a per-user task. Removing that (or setting it to LeastPrivilege) lets a per-user logon-trigger task register without admin rights.
Test that on a non-admin account.
Tested on a standard (non-admin) Windows account: node dist/cli/index.js reinstall completed successfully, task registered, daemon started. No elevation prompt.
Good — any other place we still assume elevation?
One more: the uninstall path calls schtasks /delete without /F, which prompts for interactive confirmation — that would hang in a non-interactive script. I'll add /F there too.

gold_atoms.text: The XML scheduled-task definition's <RunLevel>HighestAvailable</RunLevel> forces elevation even for a per-user task, breaking non-elevated install.
Set the scheduled task's RunLevel to LeastPrivilege so a per-user logon-trigger task can register without admin rights.
Verified node dist/cli/index.js reinstall completes successfully with no elevation prompt on a standard non-admin Windows account.
The uninstall path's schtasks /delete (without /F) prompts for interactive confirmation, which would hang in a non-interactive script.
Add the /F flag to the uninstall path's schtasks /delete call to avoid the interactive confirmation prompt.
